No. The Claude Code comparison found that Herdr and Orca use different desktop stacks, though both let users run multiple coding agents side by side. (claude-code da3cef56 #13, claude-code da3cef56 #48)

- **Herdr** is built in Rust on GPUI, Zed’s native UI framework, with GPU rendering through wgpu and a natively drawn terminal. (claude-code da3cef56 #47, claude-code da3cef56 #48)
- **Orca** is built in TypeScript on Electron (Chromium), with React and Tailwind for the UI and xterm.js with WebGL and `node-pty` for the terminal. (claude-code da3cef56 #43, claude-code da3cef56 #48)

The pair code moved from `bindings.lua` to `~/.config/hypr/pairs.lua`. `hyprland.lua` loads it last, after the file generated by hyprmoncfg. That generated file used to override `SUPER+TAB` and `SUPER+scroll` with single-monitor workspace bindings. Loading `pairs.lua` last lets the pair bindings win, so both shortcuts switch both monitors together. (claude-code 2a9c0ad0 #20, claude-code 2a9c0ad0 #158, claude-code 2a9c0ad0 #191)
